title: Split prefetch/eviction metering and burst-rate attribution for coalesced KV batches
creator: Lena Moore
description: Summary: We need a clear, auditable accounting model that separates costs and quota attribution for three distinct token sources in coalesced inference batches: (1) live tokens (non-cached), (2) opportunistic KV cache hits delivered from eviction/prefetch windows, and (3) prefetch-only tokens requested speculatively by the runtime. Problem: Current metering aggregates coalesced batches and attributes token costs and rate-limit consumption to the requesting API route without separating whether tokens were served from cache, returned as prefetch, or rehydrated after eviction. This causes incorrect billing and quota exhaustion for high-miss, high-prefetch workloads and obscures the real unit economics for customers. Goal: Implement a split accounting scheme so billing/quotas/rate-limiter attribution reflect the true token origin, while preserving batching efficiency and minimal runtime overhead.
proposed_design: 1) Per-token origin flag: augment batch metadata with a lightweight origin tag per request or token-span: LIVE | PREFETCH_SPECULATIVE | KV_REHYDRATED. The tag is derived at the time the request is enqueued/coalesced, and reconciled at emission time for KV rehydrates. 2) Attribution buckets: route-level usage will be charged for LIVE tokens. PREFETCH_SPECULATIVE tokens will be charged to a separate prefetch budget owned by the account (fallback: bill at reduced prefetch unit price if allowed), and KV_REHYDRATED tokens will be attributed to the original requesting route if within a configurable time-window, otherwise billed as a generic cache-service charge. 3) Rate-limiter integration: implement two token counters per customer: primary token counter (for LIVE) and prefetch/burst counter (for speculative prefetch + short-term rehydrates). The rate limiter will decline LIVE when primary exhausted but allow PREFETCH_SPECULATIVE up to the burst counter to maintain tail-latency SLOs. 4) Metering pipeline changes: add a pass in the metering collector that expands coalesced batch records into per-origin micro-rows before aggregation and quota reconciliation. 5) Backcompat: default policy preserves existing aggregate charges; opt-in customers can enable origin split to get detailed billing and separate prefetch budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Per-origin tags emitted for >99.9% of coalesced batches in staging and 100% in opt-in canary
Billing pipeline shows separate totals for LIVE, PREFETCH_SPECULATIVE, KV_REHYDRATED in reports and invoices
Quotas and rate limits correctly block LIVE requests when primary exhausted while allowing PREFETCH_SPECULATIVE up to configured burst limit
End-to-end latency p50/p95 change <5% for typical workloads after origin tagging overhead
Migration path documented and enabled via account feature flag; no silent double-billing in rollout
rollout_plan: Week 1: Instrumentation only in staging — emit per-origin tags and collect telemetry; do not change billing or quotas
Week 2: Enable metering pipeline expansion in internal billing job and run dry-run reconciliation against historical data
Week 3: Canary accounts opt-in to split billing and prefetch budget (small set of high-usage customers) — monitor invoices and quota behavior
Week 4: Gradual ramp to 10% of customers with opt-in; offer a migration window where customers can choose default legacy aggregation
Final: Flip opt-in toggle off to make split accounting default after sign-off from finance and billing; publish docs
telemetry_queries: SELECT origin, count(*) AS tokens, sum(token_duration_ms) AS work_ms FROM metering.expanded_batches WHERE created_at >= '{{date}}' GROUP BY origin;
SELECT customer_id, origin, sum(tokens) FROM metering.expanded_batches WHERE origin IN ('PREFETCH_SPECULATIVE','KV_REHYDRATED') GROUP BY customer_id, origin ORDER BY sum(tokens) DESC LIMIT 50;

-- Detect mismatches between batch-level and expanded totals
SELECT batch_id, batch_total_tokens, sum(expanded.tokens) AS expanded_total FROM metering.batches LEFT JOIN metering.expanded_batches expanded USING(batch_id) WHERE batch_created >= '{{date}}' GROUP BY batch_id HAVING batch_total_tokens != sum(expanded.tokens) LIMIT 100;
implementation_notes: Runtime: add origin-tag generation at coalescer where requests are grouped; minimal memory: store tag as 1-byte enum per request entry
Serving: when KV hits are satisfied at emit-time, mark those token spans as KV_REHYDRATED and reconcile origin if prefetch had already been charged
Metering: implement an expansion transformation that converts a coalesced batch record into N per-origin micro-records before aggregation; durable stream with idempotency key
Rate limiter: extend customer quota model to support two counters and a weighted fallback rule; persist counters in existing quota-store to reuse leases
Billing: finance to approve prefetch unit price and policy for retroactive adjustments during rollout
Performance: benchmark extra CPU overhead for expansion pass using real traffic simulator; aim for <1% extra CPU in collector cluster

notes_for_oncall: If customers report sudden quota exhaustion after opt-in, check the metric meter.expanded_batches.origin='LIVE' to ensure LIVE tokens are not being mis-labeled
For rate-limit surprises inspect the two counters in quota-store for discrepancies and the lease flow logs from the quota allocator
